note: 'and fall short of the glory of God' (Rom 3:23). The standard is named, and named as God's rather than as the law's.
'and are justified freely by His grace' (Rom 3:24), joined to v23 by a participle rather than begun as a new sentence.
'through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus' (Rom 3:24).
'for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,' (Rom 3:23).
'Therefore no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law.' (Rom 3:20), three verses before the verdict falls on everyone.
The verse says 'him' throughout and names nobody; 2Cor 5:18 has 'reconciled us to Himself through Christ' three verses earlier. Implied for that reason alone.
'so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God' (2Cor 5:21).
'God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf' (2Cor 5:21). The word is used twice in the verse, once of what he was made and once of what he had not known.
Said by Paul at Rom 3:23; the letter names him at Rom 1:1.
Said by Paul at 2Cor 5:21; the letter names him at 2Cor 1:1.
Said by Paul at 2Cor 8:9; the letter names him at 2Cor 1:1.

The same exchange in the same letter with wealth in the place of righteousness -- he became what we were, that we might become what he was. Paul does not connect the two verses, so the pairing is the graph's; the structure is his.
'For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor' (2Cor 8:9). Paul names the thing before describing it.
